blind_rationale: Study S649 (Gonzalez Rivas 2012) examines municipal-level progress in household in-dwelling piped water coverage across Mexican municipalities from 2000 to 2005 (N = 2,372 in Table 3; N = 2,342 in Tables 4 and 5). Although the title refers to 'indigenous municipalities' and the background mentions constitutional municipal water management (Article 115) and 1990s decentralization/privatization rules in footnotes, the actual empirical models do NOT test any legal status, formal recognition, customary-law governance (usos y costumbres), land tenure, tariff, regulation, ownership, or enforcement rule. Instead: (1) the paper's key independent variable ('indigenous', Tables 3 and 5) is strictly a demographic/ethnolinguistic composition measure—the logged census share of municipal residents in 2000 speaking an indigenous language—which fails narrow Criterion 2 (E03: sociodemographic disparity without a tested legal/administrative rule); (2) the mediating fiscal exposure in Table 5 ('Transfers pc', ln transferspc) measures cumulative 2000–2005 per-capita federal block transfers (Aportaciones Federales in constant 2002 pesos) aggregating infrastructure, health, education, and other programmes, which is a macro multi-sector intergovernmental expenditure input rather than a legal or regulatory rule governing water service access (at most a broad fiscal-allocation proxy); and (3) Model 2 (Table 4) models per-capita federal transfers as the dependent variable (predicted by indigenous share and 2000 presidential vote share), which is not a household WASH outcome (E04 if extracted). While the dependent variable in Tables 3 and 5 satisfies Criterion 4 (municipal share of households with an in-dwelling piped water network connection), neither tested predictor belongs in SWiM Family A (demographic language share is not legal status, tenure, or formal recognition), Family B (aggregate multi-sector intergovernmental fiscal transfers are not household/community WASH assistance, participation, or trust), or Family C (not utility ownership, regulatory oversight, or administrative capacity). Thus 'none_nonfit' is fully justified, and the study should be flagged for PI scope review under narrow Criterion 2 (E03).

headline_estimate_summary: Three municipality-level models in Mexico (2000-2005), all controlling for state dummies and a queen-contiguity population-weighted spatial lag (no 95% CIs printed): (1) Model 1 (Table 3, PDF p. 9 / p. 38, GLM with logit link predicting 2005 municipal share of households with in-dwelling piped water connection, N = 2,372): ln indigenous (2000 population share speaking an indigenous language) beta = -0.0310, robust SE = 0.0126, z = -2.4500, p = 0.0140 (adverse association with piped water coverage), adjusted for ln water 2000 (0.9316, SE = 0.0385, p = 0.0000), ln density (0.1411, SE = 0.0176, p = 0.0000), ln 1999 per-capita income (0.0294, SE = 0.0091, p = 0.0010), ln migration (0.3092, SE = 0.0621, p = 0.0000), spatial lag (0.0392, SE = 0.0089, p = 0.0000), and state dummies. (2) Model 2 (Table 4, PDF p. 10 / p. 39, OLS predicting ln cumulative 2000-2005 per-capita federal transfers Aportaciones Federales in constant 2002 pesos, N = 2,342, adj. R2 = 0.72): ln indigenous beta = -0.003, SE = 0.001, t = -2.800, p = 0.005; ln 2000 presidential winning-party vote share beta = 0.063, SE = 0.019, t = 3.340, p = 0.001. (3) Model 3 (Table 5, PDF p. 11 / p. 40, GLM with logit link predicting 2005 piped water coverage share, N = 2,342, same controls as Model 1 plus transfers): ln indigenous beta = -0.0305, robust SE = 0.0127, z = -2.4000, p = 0.0170; ln per-capita federal transfers (Transfers pc) beta = 0.5713, robust SE = 0.2437, z = 2.3400, p = 0.0190 (positive association with 2005 piped water coverage).
study_design_and_sample: Observational municipality-level lagged longitudinal regression study in Mexico (2000-2005) combining INEGI 2000 Population Census, 1999 Economic Census, 2005 Population Survey, and 2000-2005 Public Finances data. Unit of analysis: Mexican municipalities (2,454 total descriptive; N = 2,434 in Table 1; primary analytic samples N = 2,372 municipalities in Table 3 GLM logit-link water coverage model, and N = 2,342 municipalities in Table 4 OLS transfers model and Table 5 GLM logit-link water coverage model with transfers).
